translationRepairs: On dingyou day Hulishi galloped across Han Dewei's path and caused him to fall from his horse; enraged, the Empress Dowager had him executed.
On dingyou day Hulishi galloped across Han Derang's path and caused him to fall from his horse; enraged, the Empress Dowager had him executed.
Focus Chinese 韓德讓 names Han Derang; the English wrongly uses Han Dewei (韓德威). The proposed replacement corrects the name without other changes.
On dingyou day Hulishi charged across and startled Han Dewei's horse so that he fell; the Empress Dowager was angry and killed him.
On dingyou day Hulishi charged across and startled Han Derang's horse so that he fell; the Empress Dowager was angry and killed him.
Same unit: 韓德讓 is Han Derang, not Han Dewei. The literal repair matches the Chinese name.
On dingyou day the Empress Dowager visited Han Dewei's camp, lavished rewards on him, and had attending ministers divide into teams for backgammon to celebrate.
On dingyou day the Empress Dowager visited Han Derang's camp, lavished rewards on him, and had attending ministers divide into teams for backgammon to celebrate.
Chinese 韓德讓帳 is Han Derang's camp/tent; English Han Dewei is a wrong person. Replacement is accurate.
On dingyou day the Empress Dowager visited Han Dewei's tent, richly rewarded him, and ordered attending ministers to divide into teams for backgammon to fully enjoy themselves.
On dingyou day the Empress Dowager visited Han Derang's tent, richly rewarded him, and ordered attending ministers to divide into teams for backgammon to fully enjoy themselves.
Same unit: 韓德讓 is Han Derang, not Han Dewei. The literal repair is correct.

Chinese 上與韓德讓邀擊之 names Han Derang with the emperor; Han Dewei is incorrect.
the Emperor with Han Dewei intercepted and attacked them, killed and captured nearly all; captives were distributed to serve in the Yan army.
the Emperor with Han Derang intercepted and attacked them, killed and captured nearly all; captives were distributed to serve in the Yan army.

On renshen day marching staff adviser and Xuanzheng Hall academician Ma Dechen argued that the surrendered Song troops would never serve reliably and asked that they all be sent home.
Chinese 宣政殿 is Xuanzheng Hall; Xuanyang Hall misreads 政 as 陽. Proposed replacement is accurate.
